purpose: Adds a Remove Unused CSS per-page feature with a PHP-based CSS purging engine, caching used-CSS files per URL, background regeneration via Action Scheduler, and supporting UI/API changes.
riskRationale: Six critical bugs: (1) background regeneration reads empty global $wp_styles in non-frontend contexts, (2) tag extraction regex produces malformed output, (3) class matching uses strpos causing false positives, (4) time() versioning defeats browser caching, (5) synchronous wp_remote_get in REST endpoint causes timeouts, (6) pseudo-class stripping has fixed depth. Plus 5 important bugs including unbounded memory query and stylesheet removal that lops off external CSS. Background maintenance, REST API, browser caching, and CSS matching are all non-functional.

text: The feature follows codebase patterns well, integrates cleanly into the existing buffer pipeline, and has solid UI and tests. However, 6 critical bugs and 5 important bugs make the feature unsafe to merge — the background regeneration subsystem is entirely broken, CSS matching produces false negatives/positives, browser caching is defeated, and the REST endpoint will time out on real pages.

reasoning: Background CSS regeneration is broken in two independent ways ($wp_styles empty in AS/REST contexts, unbounded memory query in regenerate_all). CSS matching has 3 critical bugs (tag extraction, class matching, pseudo-class stripping). Browser caching is defeated by time() versioning. REST endpoint does synchronous HTTP that will timeout. These are fundamental functionality gaps, not edge cases.

message: Clean extraction of used selectors from HTML using WP_HTML_Tag_Processor — correct use of core APIs for HTML traversal, robust against malformed markup.
Lightweight CSS parser with proper handling of @media/@supports nesting, @font-face, and @keyframes — correctly manages brace-depth and preserves at-rule context.
split_selectors() correctly handles nested parentheses and brackets when comma-splitting selectors, avoiding common parser pitfalls.
is_selector_used has correct safelist prefix/wildcard matching and falls through to simple-selector matching with proper pseudo-element stripping.
maybe_apply_used_css is cleanly integrated into the existing process_buffer_only pipeline, matching the established pattern of image optimisation and CDN rewriting.
UI has clear toggle, safelist textarea, and regenerate button — matches the plan exactly, follows existing component patterns, good user experience.
4 new tests covering rendering, conditional UI states, submit payload structure, and regenerate button API call behavior — good coverage of the new feature surface.

process_background() calls get_all_css_assets() which reads global $wp_styles->queue. In Action Scheduler and REST API contexts, $wp_styles is initialized but contains only admin-enqueued styles (or is empty), not frontend CSS assets. Every background regeneration job silently produces empty used-CSS output.
suggestion: Instead of reading $wp_styles in the background process, use wp_remote_get() to fetch the frontend HTML, then extract all CSS <link> tags from the HTML response and fetch their content, following the existing Cache class's fetch_remote_css() pattern. This ensures background jobs get the same CSS as the frontend renders.

message: Tag extraction regex in matches_simple_selector() is wrong — for div.container it produces 'divcontainer' (concatenating tag and class) instead of 'div', causing tag lookups to fail for all compound selectors. Every selector like div.class, div#id, or div[attr] fails tag matching.
suggestion: Replace the regex with one that strips from the first CSS special character (., #, :, [) to the end of the tag string, then trims whitespace.

message: strpos() fallback for class matching in the compound selector loop causes extreme false positives — my-class matches not-my-class because strpos does substring matching. This means CSS rules for .sidebar will be incorrectly retained on pages that only have .not-sidebar, bloating the used-CSS output.
suggestion: Remove the strpos loop entirely and use exact class matching via isset() on the HTML classes array. Class names in selectors must match exactly — a class attribute value is space-delimited, not a substring.

message: time() is used as the cache-busting version parameter for the used-CSS stylesheet URL, which changes on every page load. This completely defeats browser caching — the browser can never reuse a cached copy because the URL changes every request.
suggestion: Use filemtime() of the saved used-CSS file to generate a stable version string that only changes when the file content changes. This enables proper browser caching while still busting on content updates.

message: The single-post regenerate REST endpoint performs synchronous wp_remote_get() with a 30-second timeout to fetch the page and generate used-CSS. REST API requests have a default 5-second timeout in many proxies/load balancers, making this guaranteed to timeout on any page with medium-to-large CSS payloads. Users will see a 500 error.
suggestion: Use Action Scheduler's as_enqueue_async_action() to queue the regeneration as a background job, returning HTTP 202 Accepted immediately. This matches the existing pattern for image conversion and is reliable regardless of page complexity.

message: Pseudo-class/element stripping regex has a hard-coded single level of nesting for arguments (e.g., :not(.a) works but :not(.a .b) fails) and runs unconditionally on every selector even when no colon is present, wasting CPU on simple selectors.
suggestion: Add a strpos() pre-check for ':' and replace the regex with one that handles simple nesting via a non-greedy approach. Single-level nesting covers the vast majority of real-world selectors.

message: regenerate_all() uses 'posts_per_page' => -1 to fetch all published post IDs at once. On sites with 100k+ posts, this returns 100k post IDs (~3MB+), then queues one Action Scheduler job per post in a tight loop. This will exhaust PHP memory on large sites and overwhelm the Action Scheduler queue with thousands of jobs enqueued from a single request.
suggestion: Use batched/paged queries (200 per batch with offset) matching the existing schedule_page_cron_jobs() pattern. Queue the first batch inline, and enqueue follow-up batches as separate scheduled actions so no single request processes more than 200 posts.

message: The preg_replace stripping all <link rel="stylesheet"> tags is too aggressive — it removes external/CDN stylesheets (Google Fonts, Typekit, etc.) whose content is never captured because they aren't in $wp_styles->queue, and it strips media-specific stylesheets regardless of their media attribute. Their CSS content is lost entirely, not just purged.
suggestion: Only remove <link> tags whose href matches a handle registered in $wp_styles->queue. Preserve any stylesheet whose URL does not correspond to a registered WP style handle. Additionally, respect the media attribute — preserve stylesheets targeting print, screen and (min-width: ...), etc. unless they apply to screen.

message: delete_used_css($url=null) — when called without a URL, looks for used-CSS files at {$this->cache_root_dir}/used-css. But files are actually stored at {$this->cache_root_dir}/{domain}/{path}/used-css.css (per-domain). The all-mode path is wrong and will never find any files. This is dead code currently, but is a trap for future callers.
suggestion: Use the same subdirectory traversal pattern as delete_all_used_css() for the all-mode branch, or delegate to delete_all_used_css() directly. Add domain-level iteration to match the actual storage layout.

message: The CSS parser uses repeated substr() calls to slice remaining input (e.g., $remaining = substr($css, $i)), creating a new string copy on every character iteration. This is O(n^2) memory/CPU — on a large combined CSS payload (commonly 200-500KB), this causes excessive memory allocation and GC pressure.
suggestion: Use an integer offset cursor instead of string slicing. Only use substr() when actually extracting a token or rule body, not as a general iteration mechanism. Parse by tracking current position with an integer index.

message: delete_all_cache_files() has a manual loop over domain directories to delete used-css.css files, then immediately calls Used_CSS::delete_all_used_css() which does the exact same traversal. The inline loop is fully redundant and will cause double I/O on every cache clear.
suggestion: Remove the manual loop (lines 967-981) and keep only the Used_CSS::delete_all_used_css() call — it already handles all subdirectory traversal including nested paths.

message: delete_all_used_css() creates $instance = new self() solely to access $this->cache_root_dir. Since cache_root_dir is always WP_CONTENT_DIR . '/cache/wppo', creating a full object instance (with domain parsing from $_SERVER, constructor side effects, and option loading) just to read a constant-like property is wasteful and fragile.
suggestion: Define a class constant or static property for the cache root directory, initialized once. Reference it directly in static methods instead of constructing an instance.

message: init_safelist() passes the safelist textarea content (CSS selector expressions like '.my-class') to Util::process_urls(), which is semantically named for URL processing and could confuse future maintainers about what processing is happening.
suggestion: Rename to or create a dedicated Util::process_textarea_lines() helper, or add an inline comment explaining that process_urls() splits on newlines and trims whitespace.

message: clear_cache($url_path) checks empty($html_file_path) || empty($css_file_path) but does not check empty($used_css_path). Though get_file_path() consistently returns '' on traversal failure for all types, omitting the used_css check is inconsistent and may cause silent skip of used-CSS cleanup in edge cases.
suggestion: Add empty($used_css_path) to the guard condition for consistency with the html and css branches.

message: Duplicated notification state management logic between handleRegenerateUsedCSS and handleSubmit — both functions set isLoading, setNotification, and setTimeout to clear the notification.
suggestion: Extract a shared helper or use a custom hook to manage the notification lifecycle consistently between both handlers.

message: get_safelist() is defined but never called anywhere in the codebase, making it dead code that adds unnecessary surface area and maintenance burden.
suggestion: Remove the method if unused, or add a @see or @todo comment documenting the intended consumer if it's reserved for future use.
